question: On genuinely new multi-intervention causal tasks, how many second calibration observations are information-theoretically necessary for sound causal answers, and what feasible saving remains against a fully TRAIN-informed exact solver? If headroom is small, do not spend compute training another representation in this domain.

domain.operator_algebra: S3 four globally persistent role permutations

domain.optional_second_public_pair: one per role, disambiguates exact operator

exact_optimizers.a: Fully TRAIN-informed exact greedy role-priority baseline, fixed score from TRAIN word-role frequencies, first pairs only until purchased, certifies all global bindings
exact_optimizers.b: Deterministic fixed-priority exact baseline, not TRAIN selected
exact_optimizers.c: Prospective mathematically optimal online expected-query decision tree, minimizes expected additional queries under UNIFORM remaining global operator assignments, without accessing the actual hidden operator
exact_optimizers.d: Full-public exact, reference upper purchase bound
exact_optimizers.e: Hindsight optimistic oracle disclosure floor for actual hidden assignment, computed by scorer after outcomes only; NEVER run as a predictive arm or counted as deployable
exact_optimizers.proof: Each online policy must return a value only when every public-consistent assignment yields identical full 3-vector of outputs. DP enumerates exactly all 2^4=16 initial assignments and every observable query outcome, no hidden oracle access to optimal policy.

qualification.go_no_go_metric: Prospective expected *online* exact policy headroom against fully TRAIN-informed exact greedy (measured across fresh DEV), plus actual realized queries and gap to hindsight floor. Continue learned cognition only if meaningful improvable headroom, not a positive result from nonlearned exact DP.
